chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ismail al-Basri, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Fuzayl! The truthful is the first one whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ratifies. He knows that he is truthful, and his soul ratifies him, knowing that he is truthful.'
ai.seo_question: What is the sign of a truthful person according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual reality of truthfulness (sidq), emphasizing that it is not merely a verbal claim but a state of being validated by Allah’s knowledge and internalized in the soul’s certainty. This concept aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of 'sidq' as a foundational virtue that bridges divine recognition with inner peace, serving as a precursor to the repayment of trusts (amanah) discussed in the chapter. The narration highlights the psychological and spiritual integrity of the truthful, whose soul bears witness to their own alignment with divine truth.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ismail Al Basry, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘O Fuzayl! The truthful is the first one whom Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Ratifies. He knows that he is truthful, and its ratification is that he comes to know that he is truthful’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Isma’il al-Basri from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “Once

abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said to me, ‘O Fudayl, the truthfulness of a truthful person is first verified by Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy. He knows that he is truthful. Then his own soul confirms; it knows his truthfulness.’”
